summary.name: FreedomBox
summary.one_liner: FreedomBox is a free software personal server that runs on cheap home hardware and lets non-experts install privacy-focused server applications such as file sharing, chat, VPN, and blog hosting.
use_cases: replace Dropbox-style file sharing at home
host a personal website or blog from home
private group chat and audio/video calls
remote VPN access to home network
home NAS for media and backups
summary.what_it_does:
FreedomBox is a private server OS that lets users install and configure server applications with a few clicks, running on hardware they choose at home. It is built on Debian and is free and open source software, supported by the non-profit FreedomBox Foundation. Listed features include file sharing, a decentralized WhatsApp-style chat, a VPN server for secure remote access and untrusted networks, a privacy-enhancing proxy, hosting for blogs or wikis, calendar and contact sync, and NAS-style media sharing and backups. The page says it is meant to keep data under the user's control rather than with tech companies.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Official part of Debian and built on GNU/Linux
Designed for non-experts with one-click style app installation
Runs on cheap hardware of the user's choice using home internet and power
Backed by the non-profit FreedomBox Foundation
caveats: A pre-built FreedomBox can be bought, which the page presents as the easiest route; it did not state a price
Page does not give hardware requirements or detailed setup steps
